chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever puts on a hair garment has entered the state of Ihram, even if he does not speak, whether little or much."

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: As for Ifrad (performing Hajj alone), it is that the pilgriff proclaims the Talbiyah for Hajj from the Miqat of his people, performing it alone from the Qiran and Umrah as well, and there is no Hady (sacrifice) upon him and no renewal of the Talbiyah at every Tawaf. Then the rituals of the Mufrid and the rituals of the Qarin are the same, there is no difference between them.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered the state of Ihram (sacred consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: Talbiyah, the recitation of 'Labbayk' during Hajm
key_terms.الْإِفْرَادُ: Ifrad, a type of Hajj where one performs Hajj alone without Umrah
key_terms.الْقَارِنِ: Al-Qarin, a pilgriff who combines Hajj and Umrah together
key_terms.بَدَنَة: A garment made of hair or wool, the wearing of which signifies entering Ihram
key_terms.طَوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.مِيقَات: Miqat, the designated stations of entry for Ihram
key_terms.هَدْي: Hady, the sacrificial animal offered by pilgrims

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on entering Ihram by wearing a hair garment and the differences between Ifrad and Qiran?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the technical validity of Ihram through the wearing of a specific garment (Badanah) without explicit verbal declaration, highlighting the flexibility in ritual intent. Shaykh al-Tusi further elucidates that the Hajj al-Mufrid requires no additional sacrifice (Hady) or Talbiyah renewal per Tawaf, noting that its core rituals are identical to those of the Hajj al-Qarin, thereby simplifying the pilgrim's obligations.
